symptom: `mxcli diff-local` printed only `Summary: 0 new, 1 modified, 0 deleted` (and `--format struct` said "(no changes)") after `alter settings constant … in configuration …` or `alter settings runtime (BcryptCost: 11)`; the same silence for navigation, project/module security, a page's or published REST service's allowed roles, an entity index, a constant's default value
cause: bsonToMDL had no case for `Settings$ProjectSettings`, so the unit fell to the generic rendering: two comment lines naming the type, identical at every revision. More generally, diff-local's renderers are lossy per doctype, and a unit whose change lies outside what its renderer prints rendered the same on both sides; the output loop then printed nothing (unified), the identical table (side) or "(no changes)" (struct) while the summary counted it
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_diff_local.go` (bsonToMDL settings case, projectSettingsBsonToMDL, constantValueMasks, unrenderedChangeNote; output via WriteDiffResults), `cmd_settings.go` (writeProjectSettingsMDL split out of describeSettings), `cmd_diff.go` (ChangedPaths, moved from mdl/scriptdiff and shared), `mdl/backend/modelsdk/parse_raw.go` (ParseProjectSettingsFromRaw)
insight: **Fix the class at the comparison, not per renderer**: git already said the bytes differ, so `Current == Proposed` on a modified unit is never "no change" — it is "the renderer is lossy here". Print what changed (property paths from the raw BSON, never values) instead of nothing; `mxcli diff` had this exact mechanism (`DiffResult.Writes`, `changedPaths`) and diff-local had simply never used it — moving the path walker into the executor gave both commands one answer. Probe before believing the reported doctype is the only one: one script per statement kind against a git-initialised app copy found nine silent unit kinds behind the two reported. The walker counted Mendix's leading int32 typed-array marker as a list item (a first grant read "1 -> 2 items"), in `mxcli diff` too. Masking a secret must keep the change visible: a constant `<masked>` on both sides diffs to nothing, so each side is rendered knowing the other's value (`<masked: old value>` / `<masked: new value>`), and the mask is deliberately not a string literal so pasted output fails to parse rather than storing "masked"
